intro.after: to balance stiffness, durability, and comfort.

items.label: Static Load:
items.body: A 75kg rider increases upper spoke tension by ~15%, while lower spokes lose tension. (De-tensioning cycle).

items.label: Heavy Riders:
items.body: Need higher base tension and thicker spokes (14G) to prevent spokes from going slack, which causes fatigue failure.

items.label: MTB / Gravel
items.body: Durability focus. Slightly lower tension for compliance and impact absorption.

items.label: Touring / Commuting
items.body: Reliability focus. Moderate tension, thicker spokes.

table.title: Recommended Drive-Side Tension (kgf)
table.note: These are baseline values for Drive-Side spokes. Non-Drive Side tension is typically 60-70% of Drive Side, determined by hub geometry. Max tension for Carbon rims is usually ~135kgf; Alloy rims ~125kgf.

steps.title: 1. Baseline Calculation
steps.body: Determine base tension range based on Rider Weight classification.

steps.title: 3. Safety Cap Check
steps.body: Ensure target does not exceed Rim Limits (Carbon 135kgf / Alloy 125kgf).

steps.title: 4. Stress Relief & Balancing
steps.body: Repeated de-stressing cycles to ensure tension does not drop after first ride.
